ns2:section.sectionText: This course examines the complex and often tragic history of relations between Christians and Jews in Europe. We will study the religious and social roots of anti-Semitism as well as cultural and political transformations that improved Christian-Jewish relations. The course spans European history from the medieval persecutions of Jews all the way to the emergence of a discourse of religious tolerance in the Enlightenment. Close consideration of the history of banishments, re-admissions, and the impact of Christian reform movements. This section for Undergraduate Students- 3 credit hours.
